payload.headline: Meta rebounds 6.55% to 597.6 into resistance; still wait for January earnings

summary.thesis: Meta is still growing sales fast, but heavy spending has cut its profit margin and free cash flow, and today's price already assumes cash-flow growth that none of the cash-flow (DCF) scenarios reach.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price or for proof in the 2027-01-27 report. Swing: no trade while the price sits just under resistance in a downtrend.
summary.act_at: Buy at 475.85; swing only after a close above 622.66

payload.happening: Meta rose 6.55% to 597.6. That put it back above the 576.61–586.24 support zone it broke in the last note, but it now sits just under resistance that starts at 607.98, and the trend is still down. The two news items were reported by The Verge: Meta Muse can shop at Walmart for Black Friday, and protesters stormed Meta offices in India. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Demand is fine. Sales grew 27.53% over the last twelve months to 241.6B, up from 189.5B. Growth is slowing, though: 26.07% year on year last quarter, against 33.08% two quarters earlier. The real change is in costs. Operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) fell to 32.86% from 43.23%. Free cash flow (cash left after spending on the business) dropped to 28.6B from 44.8B, which is only 11.86% of sales. The balance sheet moved from cash to slight net debt of -1.2B, with 83.7B of total debt, though liquidity of 82.4B means there is no funding strain. The filings also flag a 29% miss against forecasts last quarter, and profit per share is lagging sales. The core ad business is not at risk on this data, and the gross margin of 81.03% is intact. What is at risk is how much cash the business keeps. Today's headlines move sentiment only: the Walmart shopping feature is a small product step, and the India protest is a local disruption. The reported insider sales of $14.1M are a governance note, not a business change.

worth.text: There are two ways to value Meta here, and they disagree. The cash-flow model (DCF) starts from 28.6B of free cash flow and gives 243.13 (bear), 372.24 (base) and 506.03 (bull), so all three are below 597.6. To justify the current price, free cash flow would have to start growing at about 36.7% a year, which is above the model's 30% cap. Even at 30% the value is 467.76. The second method uses Meta's own price-to-sales history and gives 475.85 to 881.21, with a middle of 707.21, because sales are growing even though cash is not. On simple multiples, the stock trades at 20.4 times earnings and 6.4 times sales. That is above the peer median of 5.8, but near fair once growth is counted (0.97), and at only the 27th percentile of its own 5-year range. The whole gap between the two methods comes down to one thing: whether free cash flow recovers or stays depressed. If the operating margin fell to 24%, the DCF value would drop to 240.08.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers toward the earlier 44.8B as the heavy spending pays off, instead of staying near 28.6B.

bull: Sales are still growing fast: up 27.53% over the last twelve months, with a 3-year average of 23.92%.
The multiples are modest: 20.4 times earnings, at the 27th percentile of its own 5-year price-to-sales range, and 0.97 against peers once growth is counted.
The core product is very profitable: the gross margin is 81.03%, so the cash squeeze comes from spending choices, not from weak demand.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 28.6B from 44.8B, and every DCF value is at or below 506.03.
Operating margin fell to 32.86% from 43.23%, and the company missed forecasts last quarter by 29%.
The price implies 36.7% starting cash-flow growth. That is above the 30% cap, and even 30% growth is worth only 467.76.

levels.what: Bottom of the lower support zone (552.79–558.93). A close below it means the downtrend has resumed.
The DCF bull value. Below it, the price no longer sits above every cash-flow estimate.
Buy level: the low end of Meta's own price-to-sales history and close to the 467.76 value at 30% growth, so a purchase here does not depend on a full margin recovery.

longterm.why: At 597.6 the price is above every DCF value, the business is graded C, and cash flow is shrinking. Buying now means paying in advance for a margin recovery the reports have not yet shown.

swing.why: The bounce reclaimed 586.24, but resistance starts at 607.98, less than one average daily move (ATR 24.58) away. The 20-day average of 616.92 is falling and the trend is down. No trade until a close above 622.66, the top of the first resistance zone.

decision.timing: Options price an 11.9% move by Dec 18 and a 19.6% move by Feb 19, which includes the 2027-01-27 report. That report decides the case, so there is no long-term entry before it unless the price reaches 475.85 first.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows the operating margin climbing back toward 43.23% or free cash flow returning toward 44.8B. That would justify buying above 475.85, up toward 586.24.
A close below 552.79 opens the way to the 506.03 DCF bull value and keeps the buy level at 475.85 or lower.
A close above 636.45, the top of the 7-touch resistance zone, would break the downtrend pattern and make a swing entry possible.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, because the 6.55% rebound to 597.6 took back the 586.24 level but stopped right under resistance starting at 607.98, and free cash flow is still 28.6B against 44.8B a year earlier.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
